name: Sovereign debt stress
value: OAT–Bund ~150bp, moving either side of line
summary: France–Bund 10-year spread 154bp on the morning of 9 Nov, around the 150bp Alert line; Italy–Bund about 112bp
state: The France–Germany 10-year spread was 154bp on the morning of 9 Nov, with French yields at 4.80% (ABC Bourse), after peaking at 170bp on 22 Oct; French 10-year yields eased to about 4.75% on 11 Nov amid political and fiscal concerns (Trading Economics). The Italy–Bund spread closed at 111.7bp on 2 Nov, well inside Normal (Teleborsa). The French spread has moved either side of 150bp without holding above it, and no failed G7 auction or emergency ECB purchases was found as of 14 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: High French borrowing costs raise the cost of public debt and can feed through to mortgage and business lending rates in France. Holders of French government bonds face price swings as the spread moves around 150bp.
rubric_hit: France–Bund ~150bp, oscillating around the 150bp Alert line without holding above it; Italy–Bund 112bp < 150bp

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
